title: Reduce GPU memory & workspace: activation checkpointing, scratch buffer reuse, arena tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce peak GPU memory and transient workspace usage across common serving workloads. On multi-tenant dedicated pools we observed OOM pressure and large workspace allocations caused by per-request scratch buffers and conservative arena sizing. This PR combines three complementary changes: (1) activation checkpointing for long transformer layers with a heuristic that enables it only when expected activation memory exceeds threshold; (2) reuse and pooling of kernel scratch buffers across calls and streams to avoid repeated allocations; (3) a tuned arena allocator with per-device profiles and a lightweight compaction pass to keep worst-case fragmentation low.

What changed (high level): - Add a pluggable activation_checkpointing module with runtime heuristics and a config override (runtime config key: runtime.activation_checkpointing.enabled & .threshold_bytes). The default heuristics are conservative to avoid latency regressions. - Implement shared scratch buffer pool used by attention and FFN kernels. Pools are per-device and scoped to the arena to ensure deterministic reuse and avoid cross-stream races. - Refactor arena_allocator to introduce size-class bucketing and a compact-on-high-watermark codepath (arena.compact_threshold). Also added a simple profile loader (examples/configs/arena_tuning.yaml) with recommended values for A100/RTX6000/RTX8000. - Scheduler tweak: continuous_batcher now requests smaller per-request workspace footprints when pool contention is detected to avoid amplification. - Tests & monitoring: added perf benchmarks (tests/perf/gpu_memory_bench.cc), GPU unit tests for pool reuse, and new telemetry metrics (runtime.arena_fragmentation, runtime.scratch_pool_reuse_rate).

Performance/results: - End-to-end synthetic long-sequence generation (2048 tokens, batch=8) shows 18-30% reduction in peak GPU memory on A100 depending on model size (smaller models see ~18%, 70B-class ~28-30%). - Average per-request latency regressed +2-5% in the worst case when activation checkpointing triggers; empirical production routing shows <1.5% tail latency impact due to default heuristics. - Throughput under full utilization improved by ~12% because reduced OOMs and fewer evasive fallback allocations allow more sustained batching.

Compatibility & risk: - Activation checkpointing is opt-in by heuristics and can be fully disabled via config or per-deployment flag. - KV-cache interaction: added a guard to ensure KV cache prefetch doesn't race with scratch pool reuse; see runtime/kv_cache_integration_test. - Fragmentation compaction is triggered only when fragmentation > arena.compact_threshold to avoid extra CPU overhead. We observed no functional regressions in existing unit tests.

Rollout plan: - Canary on Dedicated GPU pool (canary group 5% traffic) for 48 hours with aggressive telemetry. - If stable, gradually increase to 25% then 100% over a week. - Feature flags present to disable activation_checkpointing and compaction if issues arise.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added for arena allocator and scratch pool - [x] Perf benchmark added and CI perf job updated - [x] Docs: short guide and recommended profiles (docs/perf/arena_tuning.md, examples/configs/arena_tuning.yaml) - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-1423 for arena work, ENG-1538 for checkpointing heuristic) - [x] Telemetry dashboards added (runtime.arena_fragmentation, runtime.scratch_pool_reuse_rate)

Related: ENG-1220 (scheduling improvements), SUP-6821 (customer OOM incident that triggered investigation)

release_notes: Reduce peak GPU memory usage via activation checkpointing heuristics, shared kernel scratch buffer pool, and arena allocator tuning. Adds new telemetry and recommended device profiles. Activation checkpointing can be disabled via runtime flag.
